subject: Post-call synthesis: Payly economics, batching/caching levers, and next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@payly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call synthesis: Payly economics, batching/caching levers, and next steps

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Below is a short synthesis of the key pain points you shared, the goals we agreed on, and the cost levers we sketched. I want to ensure we’re aligned before Marissa and I pull together a concise pilot proposal.

What you said (pain & constraints)
- Primary use: real-time transaction enrichment + fraud scoring on the authorization path (p95 latency target ~120ms).
- Budget constraint: current ML infra budget capped at ~$12k/month for inference in Q4; procurement needs a clear ROI case tied to transaction uplift.
- Sensitivity to per-token spend: volume estimate ~120M tokens/mo during peak; limited appetite for long-term model licensing.

Goals we agreed to measure
- Proof: maintain p95 latency <= 120ms on auth path for 100 req/sec spike surface.
- Economics: show a unit-cost reduction vs current CPU-based baseline using batching + KV prefix caching, targeting >=30% net cost improvement at 120M tokens/mo.
- Quality guardrail: false-positive rate for fraud signal should not increase by >1.5% vs current model.

Cost levers discussed (summary)
- Batching: exploit inference-side micro-batching during 25–100ms windows for non-blocking enrichment to reduce per-token GPU overhead.
- KV/prefix caching: cache user/session prefixes for repeat flows; expected token-level savings on ~40% of requests (you indicated a lot of repeated merchant interactions).
- Model routing: latency-aware routing to a slightly cheaper quantized variant for non-critical calls, fallback to full model for high-confidence decisions.
- Reserved capacity + modest quantization: combining a small dedicated pool (daily committed capacity) with int8+ quantization for 5–10% latency/price tradeoff.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the 120M tokens/mo estimate and the procurement runway ($12k/month)? If those are different, tell us which number is correct.
2) Can you share a small sample of conversation length distribution (histogram or raw anonymized snippets) so Karthik can estimate batching gains? We’ll treat samples as masked/anonymized.
3) If procurement requires an enterprise SOW, who on your side should we loop in (name + email)?

Deliverables from Redwood (by EOD Fri)
- Short pilot proposal: 6-week scope, metrics (latency, FP rate, unit cost), and a cost model with 3 scenarios (conservative/expected/optimistic).
- A token-economics spreadsheet with estimated monthly spend and per-1000-token price buckets (we’ll attach).

Marissa will follow up with a draft pilot SOW and an operations checklist for the auth-path integration. Karthik will produce an initial batching/caching estimate once you share the sample.

Thanks — aim to have a concise proposal in your inbox Friday.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment stubs referenced: Payly_token_econ_table.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redwood_TCO_playbook.pdf (short playbook)
From: Elena Morales <elena@payly.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@payly.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call synthesis: Payly economics, batching/caching levers, and next steps

Sean — thanks for the crisp recap. Yes, that aligns with what we discussed. Quick clarifications:

- Token volume: 120M tokens/mo is our peak estimate; a more conservative baseline is ~70M tokens/mo during steady state.
- Budget: procurement has set an internal threshold of $12k/mo for 2026 Q4, but if the pilot demonstrates >25% net savings we have an internal pathway to expand.
- Procurement contact: Ravi Singh (cc’d) is the procurement lead and will own SOW review. His calendar opens next week for a short procurement sync.

I’ll anonymize a small set of payloads (length distribution only) and drop into the Drive link you shared by EOD Thursday.

Two asks from my side before your Friday deliverable:
1) In the proposal can you separate the conservative/expected/optimistic scenarios by both cost and latency impact? We need the latency risk clearly called out.
2) On the caching assumption — can you include a short note on cache invalidation for session tokens (how we avoid stale fraud-context)?

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Product — Risk & Auth | Payly, Inc.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@payly.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ravi Singh <ravi.singh@payly.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call synthesis: Payly economics, batching/caching levers, and next steps

Hi Elena / team — thanks for confirming. Attaching a quick token-econ spreadsheet and a short TCO playbook for procurement context (see attachments). Key notes I added inside the sheet:

- Conservative scenario (70M tokens/mo): assumes minimal batching (5–10% improvement) + 20% cache hit rate -> estimated spend ~$10.8k/mo.
- Expected scenario (120M tokens/mo): assumes micro-batching (20% token reduction equivalent) + 40% cache hit -> estimated spend ~$8.4k/mo with dedicated small instance + quantized model.
- Optimistic scenario: higher cache hit (55%) + batching at 30% -> estimated spend ~$6.2k/mo and headroom for quality experiments.

On cache invalidation: Karthik drafted a short ops note — TTLs per merchant-session (default 90s), event-driven invalidation on chargebacks, and conservative versioning so we can roll forward/back without stale signals affecting scoring. I pasted that paragraph in the TCO playbook.

Ravi — copying you for procurement rhythm. If it helps, we can send a single-page SOW with a 6-week pilot (fixed price) to simplify approvals — happy to run a procurement-friendly cost breakdown.

Next steps:
- Sean & I: send the pilot proposal + SOW draft by Friday EOD (we’ll include the spreadsheet and the TCO playbook).
- Elena: upload the anonymized length distribution so Karthik can finalize batching estimates.
- Ravi: let us know the procurement docs you need in a quick list (NDA? PO? offshore vendor info?).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

If you can include those with Friday’s deliverable that will materially speed approvals.

Ravi Singh
